definitions.gloss: to swarm; to crowd; to flock; to throng
definitions.explanation: To gather in a large group around something, often in an eager or chaotic way. Used for people, animals, and insects.

examples.japanese: {蜂|はち}が{花|はな}に{群|むら}がっている。
examples.english: Bees are swarming around the flowers.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちがアイスクリームの{車|くるま}に{群|むら}がった。
examples.english: The children crowded around the ice cream truck.

examples.japanese: セールが{始|はじ}まると、{客|きゃく}が{店|みせ}の{前|まえ}に{群|むら}がった。
examples.english: When the sale started, customers thronged in front of the store.

notes:
USAGE:
An intransitive verb. The target that attracts the crowd is marked with に. Conveys a sense of many individuals converging eagerly or instinctively on one point.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {虫|むし}が{群|むら}がる (insects swarm)
- {人|ひと}が{群|むら}がる (people crowd around)
- {群|むら}がって{来|く}る (to come swarming)

GRAMMAR:
Godan verb (ら行). Te-form: {群|むら}がって. Past: {群|むら}がった. Negative: {群|むら}がらない.
